sources.assessment: Compile-time release revision and version formatting; this identifies the invoked release.
Published-channel version checking, explicit dev-launcher suppression, cached registry state and optional notices.
Checkout CLI comparison, one-shot version path, status RPC, restart receipt, notice gates and upgrade liveness refusal.
Release-to-checkout freshness and command classification; prior isolated probe covers classification.

findings: Published-version upgrade notices exist; their dev suppression is deliberate.
The one-shot --version path identifies the invoked release, not an RPC query of a running daemon.
Restart receipt verifies the requested build against the disk release stamp; this is not comparison with upstream main.
Installed upgrade refuses replacement when its selected control-plane probe reports a live daemon unless --force is used; this is not proof that every daemon sharing a release is protected.
limits: Read-only source audit. No launcher, upgrade, daemon or release command executed. No exhaustive absence claim about all status/dashboard surfaces; no current GitHub issue-state refresh. Historical incident timing and restart side effects remain separately unresolved.
